name: Joel
overview: Joel was a male Levite known as the chief of the sons of Gershom, part of the Gershonite clan descended from Gershon, son of Levi. He held a leadership role among the Levites, specifically as the son of Ladan, highlighting his place within the priestly tribe. His position is noted in the chronicles of Israel, emphasizing his significance within the Levitical family structure.
namesAndTitles: The name Joel means 'YHWH is God,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning tied to the divine name of God. It is a proper name mentioned explicitly in Scripture without indication that it was given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Joel was a descendant of Gershon and the son of Ladan, placing him firmly within the Gershonite lineage. He was also the father of Jehiel, indicating his role in continuing the Levitical family line. These relationships are clearly recorded in the books of Chronicles.
scriptureSignificance: Joel's significance lies in his leadership among the Gershonite Levites, a key group responsible for specific duties in the service of the tabernacle. His role as chief underscores the organized structure of Levitical service and the importance of family lineage in maintaining priestly responsibilities. Through his descendants, such as Jehiel, Joel's legacy contributed to the ongoing service of the Levites in Israel's worship life.
